affordance_in_statement: The Inscriber processes the rituals back-to-back in the chosen sequence... The Channeler also processes the rituals in the exact same chosen sequence... the Channeler can only commence channeling once... the Inscriber has completely finished inscribing the circle for this current ritual.
removal_suggestion: Do not describe this as a standard same-order two-machine flow shop. For example, retain the Inscriber's chosen sequence but require the Channeler to process the rituals in reverse sequence when j >= 4; this leaves all supplied examples (which have j <= 3) unchanged while eliminating Johnson's rule for the general case.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes and applies Johnson's two-machine scheduling rule: partition by p1 <= p2, sort the first group by p1 ascending and the second by p2 descending.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Both members process all rituals in the exact same chosen sequence, with each second-machine phase waiting for its corresponding first-machine phase.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly identifies the problem as Johnson's rule and uses the standard partition and sorting.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the Johnson-rule partition into p1 <= p2 and p1 > p2 groups.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The two dedicated workers form a two-machine flow shop with the same job order and nonpreemptive phases.

common_affordance: A two-machine nonpreemptive flow shop in which both machines must process the jobs in one identical order.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It uses an ad hoc pairwise comparator based on a[0] + min(a[1], b[0]) versus b[0] + min(b[1], a[0]); this is not a valid transitive implementation of Johnson's ordering rule and can produce an incorrect order.

recommended_edit: Change the scheduling mechanics so that, for j >= 4, the Channeler must process rituals in the reverse of the Inscriber's chosen sequence, while retaining the current same-order rule for j <= 3 so the immutable examples remain valid.
